s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with radiation to the jaw and diaphoresis
salient_findings: Chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
key_facts: Subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, dry cough, and sinus congestion 4 days prior to presentation
Substernal pressure that resolved spontaneously the day prior to presentation
Constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with radiation to the jaw and diaphoresis
salient_findings: Chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
key_facts: Subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, dry cough, and sinus congestion 4 days prior to presentation
Substernal pressure that resolved spontaneously the day prior to presentation
Constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

shortlist.label: Myopericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein, normal coronary arteries, and ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression suggest inflammation of the heart

shortlist.label: Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pressure radiating to the jaw, diaphoresis, and ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression are consistent with pericardial inflammation

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin level, normal coronary arteries, and symptoms of chest pressure and diaphoresis suggest inflammation of the heart muscle

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin level and chest pressure radiating to the jaw are consistent with myocardial infarction, although normal coronary arteries on angiography make this less likely

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Symptoms of chest pressure, diaphoresis, and vomiting, along with elevated troponin level and normal coronary arteries, are consistent with stress-induced cardiomyopathy

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest pressure, recent history of subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, dry cough, and sinus congestion, along with elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein, and ECG findings of ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression, is most consistent with myopericarditis, which can involve both the myocardium and pericardium.

rejected.label: Pericarditis
rejected.why: While pericarditis could explain some of the ECG findings and chest pain, the elevated troponin level suggests myocardial involvement, which is not typical of pericarditis alone.

rejected.label: Myocarditis
rejected.why: Myocarditis could explain the elevated troponin and some ECG findings, but the presence of PR-segment depression and ST-segment elevations in leads II, III, and aVF, along with the clinical presentation, suggests involvement of the pericardium as well.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: The normal coronary angiography results make acute myocardial infarction unlikely, as this condition is typically associated with significant coronary artery disease.

rejected.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and diagnostic findings do not align well with takotsubo cardiomyopathy, which typically involves significant left ventricular dysfunction and a distinct 'balloon-like' appearance on echocardiography, neither of which were observed in this case.
